s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly growing vascular tumor on the scalp
salient_findings: 8-mm red, firm, mobile nodule on the left temporal scalp
Irregular red lacunae with irregular vessels and absence of septa on dermoscopic evaluation
Well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor with ectatic thin-walled vessels and intravascular branching papillary structures on histopathology
key_facts: The patient is a man in his 40s
The patient has no significant medical history
The tumor is located on the left temporal scalp
The tumor is 8-mm in size
The tumor is red, firm, and mobile
Dermoscopic evaluation shows irregular red lacunae and irregular vessels
Histopathology shows a well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor
The tumor extends to the superficial subcutaneous tissue
The tumor is composed of ectatic thin-walled vessels with intravascular branching papillary structures
The endothelial cells have numerous intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules
PAS staining is positive for hyaline globules in the cytoplasm of endothelial cells
Tumor vessels are positive for CD-31 and negative for D2-40 and HHV-8

shortlist.label: Dabska tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Matches dermoscopic and histopathological findings of a vascular tumor with intravascular papillary structures and hyaline globules

shortlist.label: Papillary intralymphatic angioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similar histopathological features, including papillary structures and positive CD-31 staining

shortlist.label: Glomeruloid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by ectatic vessels and intracytoplasmic hyaline globules, consistent with the patient's histopathology

shortlist.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Features retiform vascular channels and papillary structures, similar to the patient's tumor

shortlist.label: Hobnail hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with hobnail-like endothelial cells and intravascular papillary structures, consistent with the patient's histopathological findings

raw.rationale: The presence of intravascular branching papillary structures, ectatic thin-walled vessels, and endothelial cells with numerous intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules, which are positive for PAS staining, are characteristic features of Dabska tumor.

rejected.label: Papillary intralymphatic angioendothelioma
rejected.why: This condition typically involves lymphatic vessels and is positive for D2-40, which is not the case in this patient.

rejected.label: Glomeruloid hemangioma
rejected.why: Glomeruloid hemangioma is associated with POEMS syndrome, which is not mentioned in the patient's history.

rejected.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: This condition typically has a retiform pattern and is not characterized by the presence of intracytoplasmic hyaline globules.

rejected.label: Hobnail hemangioma
rejected.why: Hobnail hemangioma typically has a distinctive hobnail appearance and is not characterized by the presence of intravascular branching papillary structures.
